# About the Herald
[italic]The Colony Herald is the independent press of Albacetire. It answers to its readers and to nobody else.[/italic]
## How We Started In 2168 the gas came up out of Drill Site 68-B and the official count of the dead stalled for days. A handful of township clerks and out-of-work miners started pinning hand-printed sheets to the union hall door: every name they could confirm, block by block, with the shift each miner had been working. Those sheets were the first editions of the Herald.
We still print a paper sheet for the mess halls and the dome workers who would rather hold something in their hands. Everyone else reads us here on the net, free of charge.
## What We Promise - [bold]Names, not numbers.[/bold] When people are hurt or killed, we find out who they were. - [bold]No Company money.[/bold] The Herald takes no advertising or grants from Weyland-Yutani or any other firm with holdings on Albacetire. - [bold]Sources stay hidden.[/bold] We have never given up a source to the garrison, the Marshals or a corporate liaison, and we never will. - [bold]Corrections up front.[/bold] When we get it wrong, the correction goes at the top of the page, not the bottom.
## Who Writes It The Herald is filed by one accredited colony journalist at a time, working from the press office in the township and from wherever the story happens to be. Garrison officers have called us dissident sympathisers. Dissidents have called us garrison stenographers. We take both as a sign we are doing the work.
## Talking Back Every story on the front page is open for comment, and the correspondent reads all of them. Tips go to the journalist in person. For official statements, see the [netlink="Colony Administration" link="admin.colony.gov"] or [netlink="Garrison Command" link="command.govfor.mil"], then come back here to read what they left out.
